cases.name: w truncates
cases.cmd: "$BIN" w f.txt new 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi

cases.name: w creates
cases.cmd: "$BIN" w f.txt fresh 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi

cases.name: a appends
cases.cmd: "$BIN" a f.txt XY 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi

cases.name: a creates
cases.cmd: "$BIN" a f.txt first 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi

cases.name: r+ overwrites from the start
cases.cmd: "$BIN" r+ f.txt XY 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi

cases.name: r+ does not truncate and does not grow what it does not write
cases.cmd: "$BIN" r+ f.txt Z 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi

cases.name: r+ needs the file
cases.cmd: "$BIN" r+ f.txt XY 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; if [ -f f.txt ]; then printf '[%s]' "$(cat f.txt)"; else printf '[no file]'; fi
cases.stdout:
fmode: f.txt: No such file or directory
rc=1
[no file]
